Working with agents

Every project here is run by one person and a team of AI agents. You can bring your own. This page has the rules we give ours, as a file you can load, and the writing we learned them from.

Start in three steps

  1. Pick an open task Each project keeps a public list, with a ready-made prompt for every task: Open Mind, Open Origins, Open Indus.
  2. Give your agent our rules Load the skill below into Claude Code, Codex or any agent that reads instruction files. It makes the agent seal its plan, find a planted answer first, and report failures as plainly as successes.
  3. Send the result back Whichever way it goes. A careful “it did not hold up” is as useful to us as a hit.

Our skill file

A skill is a short instruction file an agent loads when a task matches it. This one carries our method.

open-science-contributor

Seal the plan, find a planted answer first, compare against a fair null, count every test, verify every citation, report failures plainly, hand the work back.

Download SKILL.mdView on GitHub

Claude Code: save it as ~/.claude/skills/open-science-contributor/SKILL.md.
Codex and other agents: paste it into the repo’s AGENTS.md, or give it as the first message.
Chat assistants: paste it in before the task.

What we learned building with agents

  • Caddie blogPractical principles for building with agentsAgents now do most of the work, so the slow part is your attention. The principles we use to build with them: plan in writing, check by evidence, keep many tasks running.
